candidate_relations.reason: Odontogenic myxoma is a mesenchymal odontogenic neoplasm, not a complex odontoma.
A complex odontoma is a benign odontogenic tumor-like hamartomatous lesion, while “bone tumor” omits its odontogenic nature and complex subtype.
A dentigerous cyst is a cyst associated with an unerupted tooth, not the dense amorphous dental-tissue mass of a complex odontoma.
Calcifying epithelial odontogenic tumor is a distinct neoplasm and does not equal complex odontoma.
Odontogenic ghost cell tumor is a distinct ghost-cell lesion rather than a complex odontoma.
Cherubism is an inherited bilateral fibro-osseous jaw condition, unlike this localized calcified odontoma.
Dental infection could relate to the presenting cellulitis but does not account for the longstanding dense calcified maxillary lesion.
Cemento-ossifying fibroma is a distinct fibro-osseous lesion, not a complex odontoma composed of disorganized dental tissues.
Complex odontoma falls within the odontogenic tumor/hamartoma family, but the candidate omits the required complex odontoma subtype.
The candidate exactly matches the benchmark diagnosis of complex odontoma.
Fibro-osseous lesion denotes replacement of bone by fibrous and mineralized tissue and is not the diagnostic category of complex odontoma.
Central giant cell granuloma is typically an expansile radiolucent giant-cell lesion, not a dense amorphous complex odontoma.
Osteosarcoma is a malignant osteoid-producing tumor and is not equivalent to the benign complex odontoma benchmark.
Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor is a distinct epithelial odontogenic tumor rather than a complex odontoma.
Odontogenic keratocyst is a keratinizing cyst and does not match the dense calcified dental-tissue lesion.
The maxillary location is compatible, but calling the lesion a cyst conflicts with the solid, densely calcified complex odontoma diagnosis.
